The card adds the degrees to 12, divides by 5 nodes, and gives the average degree 2.4." width="100%"} For directed graphs, this returns the average of (in-degree + out-degree). For undirected graphs, each edge contributes to the degree of both endpoints. In both cases the result equals `2 * edges / nodes`, since every edge adds one to the degree of each of its two endpoints. Average degree is a single-number summary of how densely connected a network is, which makes it handy for: - comparing the connectivity of networks of different sizes (unlike edge counts) - sanity-checking a generated or imported graph against an expected density - choosing parameters for random-graph models that should match a real network A single average can hide a lot: a five-node star and a five-node path both have an average degree of `1.6` but very different structures. Look at `degree_distribution()` for the full picture. Edge weights are ignored, parallel edges each count, and an empty graph gives `0.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean degree value across all nodes. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~aggregate_degree`) : Mean, median, and other degree summaries over chosen nodes. [](`~degree_distribution`) : How many nodes have each degree. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Every node in a 4-cycle has exactly two neighbors, so the average degree comes out to exactly `2.0`: ::: {#833d25ef .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) graph.average_degree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2.0 ``` ::: ::: A five-node star has four edges, so its average degree is `2 * 4 / 5 = 1.6`, even though the hub has degree `4` and every other node has degree `1`: ::: {#13c20b69 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5).average_degree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1.6 ``` ::: :::
